title: The Rough Horizon
premise: Oscar Kavanagh, a railroad engineer haunted by the memory of a bridge collapse that killed his crew, drifts along closed lines in the high interior, mapping what the railway abandoned. When a government survey team disappears near the headwaters of the Sable River — leaving their instruments set up, their tent pitched, and no tracks in any direction — Oscar is the only man with the terrain knowledge and the motive to go looking. His search becomes a race against expiring concession permits, against a company man who wants the valley erased from every map, and against his own growing bond with Ilsa, the surveyor's daughter who refuses to accept a closed file. Following the river upstream, Oscar discovers the surveyors were silenced because their readings would have exposed the company's fraudulent mineral claims, and that the missing team leader is alive, hiding in the source country he refused to falsify. In the end Oscar must choose between the safe, moving life he has built and standing still long enough to testify — and he stays, delivering the survey, saving the man, and finding in one small valley town the belonging he never let himself want.
about_author: Jonah Joubert is the pen name of a former track surveyor who spent a decade working remote lines across the interior before turning to fiction. He writes from a small house near a river, where he claims the water still tells him which way the maps lie.

chapters.title: The Man Who Keeps Moving
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He walks a decommissioned spur line, checking rails no train will ever run on, and takes a contract from the railway company to survey closed lines before the concession lapses. Flashbacks reveal the bridge collapse that made him a man who never stops. Emotional beat: restless avoidance dressed as purpose.

chapters.title: Gear With No Owners
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At a waystation he finds the survey team's abandoned camp — instruments still leveled, a kettle half-full of tea, no tracks leaving in any direction. A company clerk warns him off with too much politeness. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; the map of closed lines suddenly has a gap in it.

chapters.title: Ilsa Refuses the File
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The surveyor's daughter arrives at the waystation demanding answers; the government office has declared her father's team 'closed.' She and Oscar clash, then strike a bargain: he knows the river, she knows her father's methods. Emotional beat: two griefs recognizing each other and mistrusting the recognition.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The two push up the Sable through gorge country, following the team's instrument marks — each station logged, each log increasingly strange, elevations that don't match the official maps. A company patrol boat passes below, searching the wrong direction. Emotional beat: the river as both path and interrogation.

chapters.title: The Second Camp
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. They find the team's second camp, ransacked but not robbed — only the notebooks taken. Ilsa finds a page her father hid inside a theodolite case, half a reading and half a message: 'the source is the proof.' Emotional beat: hope and horror entwined; the disappearance was designed.

chapters.title: Company Man
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The patrol catches up: Mr. Aldous Crane, the company's land agent, offers Oscar a lucrative contract to certify the valley as worthless and forget what he's seen. Oscar recognizes the transaction — the same arithmetic that let a rotten bridge stand. He refuses. Emotional beat: the past arriving to collect its debt.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Above the last marked station the valley closes into a hidden basin where the river rises from a cave mouth — and there they find the team leader, alive, half-feral, guarding his field books. The readings prove the ore body runs under land the company already sold twice. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear; the truth is worth killing for.

chapters.title: What the River Takes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Crane's men burn the second camp and seal the gorge trail, trapping them above the falls. The escape downriver costs Oscar nearly everything — his instruments, his map, nearly his life — and in the worst moment Ilsa's hand in his is the only fixed point. Emotional beat: love against duty, chosen in the water.

chapters.title: The Permit Expires
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They reach the railway town as the concession lapses at midnight; Crane's claim dies with it, but so does the company's leverage — and its patience. Oscar delivers the field books to the government assayer and signs his name as witness, standing still in front of a room for the first time since the bridge. Emotional beat: the climax of stillness; testimony as courage.

chapters.title: A Line Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Spring: the valley town petitions for a branch line, and Oscar — hired to survey a line that will actually be built — stays. He visits the graves of his old crew and, for the first time, speaks to them. He and Ilsa walk the river's edge together. Emotional beat: belonging earned, memory carried rather than fled from.
